text:
SOURCE-ASSISTED READING, 22 September 2026

This revises selected passages after exposure to the earlier F-ahiy report and the sources listed below. It does not replace the frozen image-only response. Reading and comparison were performed by a Codex model, exact identifier unavailable, with no human palaeographic review. Full images a_rot.jpg and b_rot.jpg were inspected for layout; detailed excerpts use aL0.jpg, aR1.jpg, bR0.jpg. These are overlapping derivatives of the two sides, not additional witnesses.

The initial image-001.png represents aL0.jpg, an interior upper band of side A's left column. Counting its clipped first physical line, its lines 2–7 correspond to lines 4–9 of that column counted from the first extant line in a_rot.jpg. It is not the top of the column.

Side A, left column, aL0.jpg (same physical band as initial image-001.png):
03 [earlier part not revised] ... Modest-
04 ia tocius vite ornatu(m) tollit. id(em) e. Et de off(ici)o ei(us)? et utilita-
05 te. lib(ro) de dog(ma)te ph(ilosoph)or(um) [reference uncertain]. Modestia cultu(m) et motu(m) et om(n)em
06 n(ost)r(a)m occupat(i)onem ult(ra) defectu(m)? et cit(ra) excessu(m) sistit. unde
07 Modestia est in a(n)i(m)o (con)tine(n)s mod(er)atio cupiditatu(m). tullio? 2?

The sentence spanning 05–06 parallels Moralium dogma philosophorum, ed. John Holmberg (1929), Latin text p. 42, De modestia, lines 1–2: https://www.dbnl.org/tekst/_mor004mora02_01/_mor004mora02_01.pdf (PDF page 102, zero-based page 101). Edition text was read through extracted text; a screenshot request failed. Source has 'Modestia est ... sistere'; manuscript appears to omit est and to end sistit. The source assists defectum and citra, but defectum remains uncertain in the image. The old decentiam/contra reconstruction should not stand as a confident transcription. The preceding reference names liber de dogmate philosophorum, but its syntactic attachment and numeral are not settled.

The ending in 04 parallels Ambrose, De officiis I.45 §218, 'eam quae totius vitae ornatum attollit modestiam', checked in https://la.wikisource.org/wiki/De_officiis_ministrorum . The manuscript shows tollit, not a securely visible attollit. Do not silently emend it. The previously cited I.18 is not the locus of the checked wording. Line 07 is not validated by this source comparison; its attribution and the apparent modestia/temperantia issue remain open.

Side A, right column, aR1.jpg, lines counted from its clipped top row:
05 mu(n)dus ante me(n)dicos. J(e)r(onimus)? ad heliodor(um) x. ep(istola)? xii? g. prima v(ir)tus mo-
06 nachi est (con)te(m)pne(re) ho(m)i(nu)m iudicia. et s(em)p(er) ap(osto)li recordari dice(n)tis
07 Si ad(huc) ho(m)i(n)ib(us) placere(m) x(rist)i s(er)vus no(n) esse(m). J(e)r(onimus)? ad pa(m)machiu(m).
Separate boxed continuation beside the following Mons line: xi? ep(istola)? vi? a.

This is the last quotation before the Mons heading, roughly the upper third of side A. The cropped beginning of 05 completes the preceding excerpt; it is not part of 'prima virtus'. Jerome Ep. 66.6, ad Pammachium, was checked in the Latin transcription at https://patrologia-lib.ru/patrolog/hieronym/epist/epist03.htm . There the order is 'Prima virtus est Monachi'; the manuscript reads 'prima virtus monachi est'. The manuscript's placerem agrees with the displayed main text, which also records placere vellem as an alternative. This is a source-layer identification. The same saying occurs in Manipulus florum, Monachus f, checked at https://manipulus-project.wlu.ca/lemmata/Monachus.html . It therefore cannot identify the compiling work.

The preceding ditiores / paupere Christo / locuplete diabolo / mundus ante mendicos sequence in aR1.jpg was also compared with Jerome Ep. 60.11 at the same patrologia-lib.ru URL. The manuscript has a compressed, altered form (including sunt seculares and possident omnia, against fuerant saeculares and possideant opes in the displayed source). This additional source connection does not identify the collection either. A complete diplomatic transcription of that preceding sequence has not been certified.

Side B, right column, bR0.jpg; lines counted from its first main-text row:
02 Q(uo)d mala mors no(n) e(st) q(uam) vita bona p(re)cessit. na(m) mala(m) mortem
03 facit q(uo)d ea(m) sequitur. no(n) q(uo)d p(re)cedit. i de civit(ate) x? d. g. [next item omitted]

These are near the top of the right column. bR0.jpg is a crop of b_rot.jpg at (1260,180)–(2420,900), as recorded in the cached crop script. Augustine, De civitate Dei I.11, was checked in https://www.thelatinlibrary.com/augustine/civ1.shtml and corroborated in https://www.logicmuseum.com/wiki/Authors/Augustine/City_of_God/City_of_God_Book_I . The source begins 'Mala mors putanda non est' and continues 'Neque enim facit malam mortem, nisi quod sequitur mortem'. The manuscript recasts it as a Quod summary, omits putanda, changes word order, and adds the explicit contrast non quod precedit. Its citation numeral is left x? rather than silently changed to the modern chapter XI.

All expansions in parentheses are editorial. Ellipses and bracketed notices indicate omitted or uncertain material, not source-based restoration. No secure deletion or insertion was identified in these selected phrases. The boxed reference after the Jerome extract is kept separate. Most of both sides, including the lower Mors passages and natural-philosophical material, has not been transcribed or compared word by word in this pass.

Compiler check: https://manipulus-project.wlu.ca/browse.html lists Modestia, Monachus, Mors consecutively in the relevant section, unlike the fragment's intervening Moyses, Mollis, Mons, Monstra and side B's Mora, Morbus. Monachus f shares the Jerome saying but its surrounding excerpt arrangement does not reproduce the inspected manuscript sequence. This argues against a straightforward copy of the standard edited Manipulus; dependence, rearrangement, or mixed compilation is not excluded. Modestia's entry failed to load and was not compared. No candidate entry from Jean de Fayt, Flores paradisi, or another tabula was inspected. No comprehensive lexicon/distinctiones exclusions are established.

Result: PARTIAL, medium confidence for an alphabetical collection of auctoritates with directly checked Moralium dogma, Ambrose, Jerome, and Augustine source layers; compiler and work title unresolved. Identification confidence does not assess transcription accuracy.
